text:
taylor: Quick sync — I'm refining the "adaptive resume anchor" proposal. Problem: long streams + multi-hop retries cause wasted re-generation and messy duplicates. Idea: emit compact anchors (seq, epoch, anchor-hash, resume_blob) periodically; edge keeps a single anchor per active stream and can request a suffix using resume_blob.
erin: How is anchor different from the checkpoints / pulses we've been iterating on?
taylor: Two diffs: 1) anchors include a compact rolling-anchor (not full prefix hash) that's cheap to compute in a streaming way, designed to be verifiable by the runtime without keeping full prefix state. 2) adaptive backoff: gateway uses anchors to decide whether to attempt resume or immediately hedge based on recent resume success rates and tail latency signals.
marco: If the runtime accepts a resume_blob, does it guarantee no duplicate tokens? What about partial overlap during race with an in-flight original stream?
taylor: Contract: resume_blob contains monotonic seq N. When gateway asks resume(blob, N), runtime will only stream tokens with seq > N. The gateway dedupes by last_emitted_seq and drops anything <= that seq. For races where both original and resumed suffixs overlap, gateway merges by seq and ensures ordering. That avoids double-emit beyond the seq boundary.
erin: Gateway still needs to keep per-stream last_emitted_seq and last_anchor_blob — memory O(1) per stream. Concern: at very high concurrency that still adds up.
taylor: We cap active resumable streams via a soft threshold. Above that threshold gateway enters best-effort mode where it doesn't store anchors (fail-open) and falls back to hedging policy. We'll make threshold configurable per tier.
marco: How do we avoid replay or malicious resume_blobs?
taylor: resume_blob is HMAC-signed by the serving runtime, includes stream-id, seq, epoch, and expiry. Gateway verifies signature before attempting resume. Runtime rejects expired/blind blobs. We rotate signing keys and record resume_reject_expires etc.
erin: Adaptive backoff details?
taylor: Gateway tracks a small moving window per-route: resume_success_rate, avg_resume_latency, duplicate_incidents. If resume_success_rate > S (config), prefer_resume; if below, gateway prefers_hedge or prefer_restart. Also, if tail-latency is high and resume latency is low, prefer resume to save tokens. We'll expose knobs: resume_threshold, hedging_threshold, max_resume_attempts.
marco: Transport-wise for gRPC we need a side-channel frame; for HTTP chunked we can embed anchor headers in chunk preface. Provide examples in RFC.
erin: Billing: anchors are metadata; only re-generated tokens are billed. But if resume fails repeatedly, we could still trigger full replays which are billed. Need quotas to prevent abuse.
taylor: We'll add per-tenant/per-client caps on resume attempts and a per-stream max_resume_attempts counter. Also an exponential backoff for resume attempts on failure.
marco: Observability and SLOs: resume_attempts, resume_success, resume_reject_reason, resume_latency_ms, duplicate_emit_count, streams_in_resume_mode. Also a meter for when gateway enters fail-open due to hitting resume thresholds.
erin: What about model determinism? If sampling randomness differs between the original and resumed suffix (e.g., different RNG seed), we might diverge. Does runtime need to guarantee determinism for resumable mode?
taylor: Yes: resumable-serving contract requires deterministic continuation for resumes. Practically, runtime will supply a seed in the resume_blob or force deterministic sampling path when emitting anchors. Models that cannot guarantee this are marked non-resumable and will fall back to hedging. We'll list these in model catalog metadata.
marco: Edge case: client reads partial tokens (streaming bytes) and retry happens; dedup by seq is fine, but what about clients that re-render tokens differently (e.g., tokenization differences)?
erin: We should document that resume only works at token-boundary semantics rather than byte boundaries and clients should accept token-level deduping. For streaming text, gateways will ensure atomic token emits when possible.
taylor: Prototype plan: 1) implement anchor emission in gateway shim (opt-in header X-Anchor-Enable: 1), 2) runtime shim to sign blobs + support /resume endpoint, 3) gateway resume flow with merge/dedupe logic + adaptive policy, 4) perf sims and staging canary behind feature-flag.
marco: Perf sims to run: client RTT 300/600/900ms, model chunk 250/700ms, concurrency sweep 1k -> 50k, compare strategies: no-resume, resume-without-adaptive, resume-adaptive. We'll tune anchor interval and max_resume_attempts.
erin: Security additions: rotate runtime signing keys; validate blob TTL; rate-limit resumes by tenant and IP; sample logging of resume payloads (redacted) for debugging.
marco: One more ops concern: how to gracefully degrade if the runtime-side resume api goes down mid-flight?
taylor: Gateway will fallback to configured policy: either start hedged fresh request, or fast-fail to client depending on route policy. We'll add health-check instrumentation: if runtime resume failures spike, mark runtime as resume-disabled and switch modes.
ops-bot: canary: anchor-resume feature-flag enabled in staging: gateway-canary-2025-02-11 :white_check_mark:
marco: Ok, this looks actionable. Please add wire examples and the adaptive policy pseudocode to the RFC appendix.
erin: I'll own the perf sims and the memory/cost tables for the RFC.
taylor: Great — I'll update the RFC with pseudocode and prototyping checklist. Thanks everyone. :rocket:
